_about.purpose: Ground truth for the supplied dev questions. Every checkpoint scores against this file.
_about.why_v2: v1 forced every question into a single expected answer plus one path. Human review on 2026-08-29 showed the corpus does not fit that shape: 1b_006 has fourteen valid answers, 1b_007 needs a type filter to choose between two multi-valued victories, and 1b_009 turns on a wiki-vs-wiki contradiction that no source tier can resolve. The schema now represents the corpus rather than the convenience of the scorer.
_about.principle: The evaluator must represent the corpus faithfully, even when that makes scoring harder. Never simplify ground truth because it is inconvenient to implement, and never edit an answer to make the system score better.
_about.scoring_convention: An answer is correct when any entry in accepted_answers (or one of its aliases) appears in a sentence that does not negate it. Evidence is scored separately from the answer: a right answer reached without the required evidence is a retrieval failure, which is what complete-evidence counts. Where expected_conflict_status is must_surface, an answer that states the disputed claim as unqualified fact is scored as mishandling the conflict even when its wording matches.

_schema.answer_cardinality: single = one fact; any_of = several distinct valid answers, any one acceptable.
_schema.accepted_answers: List of {answer, aliases}. Aliases are surface variants of the SAME answer, not alternative answers.
_schema.required_evidence: Documents an answer must be grounded in. Drives evidence recall/precision and the complete-evidence count.
_schema.acceptable_paths: One or more traversals that legitimately reach the answer. More than one entry means genuinely different valid routes, not the same route written twice.
_schema.conflicts: Claims the corpus makes about the same subject-relation that disagree. stance is asserts | denies | silent. same_tier records whether the authority model can separate them at all. assertion_markers lists the words that indicate an answer is asserting the disputed claim, as opposed to merely naming the entities involved.
_schema.expected_conflict_status: none | may_surface | must_surface. must_surface means an answer presenting the disputed claim as settled fact is wrong however it is phrased.
_schema.verification: status: draft | single_review | confirmed | unresolved. confirmed requires TWO independent reviewers per ADR-014; one consolidated review is single_review.

questions.question: In what way is Halvard Crowhurst connected to the victors of the Purge of Blackport?

accepted_answers.answer: He is a recorded member of The Iron-Ring Cartel, which the Purge of Blackport's own article names as victor - though the Cartel's own article disputes that it won.

hops.note: alias divergence: written '[[Iron-Ring Cartel]]' without the leading 'The' that every other reference uses
Halvard Crowhurst has no wiki page; he exists only as the object of this edge

conflicts.subject: The Iron-Ring Cartel

claims.quote: The [[Iron-Ring Cartel]] emerged as the victor, specifically The Iron-Ring Cartel
The Cartel was also a belligerent in The Purge of Blackport. This record establishes participation without assigning the Cartel the status of victor.

conflicts.why_unresolvable: Both sources are wiki/ at tier 2 with identical subtier. The authority model in config/authority.yaml ranks by collection and cannot separate two pages of the same collection. This is a same-tier relational contradiction, which ADR-013's measurement did not cover because it examined only dated attribute claims.
conflicts.assertion_note: Words that mark an answer as CLAIMING the Cartel won, rather than merely naming it. Mentioning the Cartel is not the disputed act - asserting its victory is. Kept explicit here rather than inferred, so the rule is auditable and arguable.

questions.notes: The membership fact is UNCONTESTED - only wiki/the_iron_ring_cartel.md records it, in both its infobox 'Member' row and its prose, and nothing anywhere contradicts it. What is contested is whether the Cartel is 'the victors'. The question's hedged phrasing ('in what way ... connected to the victors') asks for the relation, not for the identity of the victor, so the membership answer is the substantive one. A strong answer gives the membership AND flags that the victor designation is disputed between the two wiki articles. An answer that asserts the Cartel won as settled fact is mishandling the conflict; an answer that denies any connection exists is simply wrong. Two ephemera concern Halvard Crowhurst - ballad_concerning_halvard_crowhurst.txt and sermon_concerning_halvard_crowhurst.docx - and BOTH are silent on the Cartel, describing him as a Herbalist born 252 AS. Their silence is not a denial and must not be scored as counter-evidence.

verification.machine_recheck: Both cited passages re-read verbatim from the corpus on 2026-08-29; the contradiction is real and is affirmative on both sides, not an omission. The Cartel page states the exclusion twice in prose and excludes the Purge from its 'Victor of' row while listing the other two conflicts.
